beats.narration: It can. The custom zip exports a Canvas cartridge — upload it, and your course is standing: modules, videos, exams, in place. Here's delivery, end to end.
The format is dot I M S C C — Canvas's own import format. No integration project, no I T ticket queue, no vendor review to schedule. Upload, confirm, teach.
If you want humans in the room, we deliver custom training and workshops ourselves — your team, your cases, our instructors.
Or white-label it: we build the workshop, your experts deliver it, and your brand carries it. Your bench gets the material. Your clients see you.
Now predict the total lock-in here — the platform fee, the seat license, the annual renewal. Count it up. Take a second.

Zero. The cartridge is a file you own. The zip is a folder you own. The rights travel with them. If we disappeared tomorrow, your course keeps running — which is exactly how course material should work.

beats.narration: AI plus one, in ninety seconds. Every course we make has a canonical version you can get today for about a dollar — and a custom version we build for you, that you own the rights to make yours. And it all comes from a nonprofit, so every purchase funds the mission. Here's the whole offer.

The canonical layer first. Every course is a textbook on Kindle for one dollar — free on Kindle Unlimited. Every lecture is on our YouTube, free. Every slide deck runs as a voiced, animated page on our site. That's not a sample. That's the whole course.

When you need your own version — your program, your examples, your name on it — you email info at humanitarians dot A I. We quote a price. You get a zip: the base videos, the exams, and the rights to transform it into your book, your course, your workshop.

The zip opens in any C L I — Claude Code, Codex, whichever you use. Point your tools at it and start editing: rename, reorder, rewrite, rebrand. You're not locked to our software, because there isn't any.
Quick check before the next part. If your world is a university learning system, guess what the zip exports to. Got a guess?

Canvas. The zip exports a dot I M S C C cartridge you upload directly — modules, videos, exams, in place. And if you'd rather we run it: custom training, or a white-label workshop your own experts deliver.

props.command: is the textbook really a dollar?
output: audit the base before you buy

beats.narration: Yes — a dollar, on purpose. Here's why the canonical version of every course is priced like a coffee tip, and what you actually get for it.
One dollar on Kindle — free if you have Kindle Unlimited. Every course. And it's the full canonical textbook, not a teaser chapter with an upsell at the end.
The lectures are free on the Humanitarians AI YouTube — the complete course in video, public. Assign it to a class, binge it yourself, check our teaching before you spend anything.
The slide decks run on our site as voiced, animated pages — every deck narrated, every build animated, right in the browser. No download, no license key, no viewer to install.
So predict the business logic: why would we price the canon at a dollar, when the custom versions are what pay for the work? Take a second.

Because the canon is the audit. You can read the book, watch the course, and hear the decks before you ever email us — so when you buy a custom version, you know exactly what the base is. No demo call. And we're a five-oh-one-C-three: on the canon, reach matters more than margin.

beats.narration: You can — and it ends with a zip you own the rights to transform. Here's the whole path, from one email to your course.
Step one: email info at humanitarians dot A I. Tell us the course, your audience, and what custom means for you. We quote a price for your version. No subscription, no platform fee — a quote.
What ships: the base videos, the exam banks, and — the part that matters — the rights to transform them. Into your book. Your course. Your workshop. Your brand on it.
It opens in any C L I — Claude Code, Codex, next year's tool. Rewrite the examples for your industry, cut what you don't teach, add what you do. Our content, your judgment.
Before the reveal, one question: what's the one thing we don't sell you? Think about what stays out of the zip — and what was never ours in the first place.

The judgment. We sell the starting point — vetted videos, tested exams — but what to teach, what to cut, what your learners actually need: that was never ours to sell. The zip makes you faster. It does not make you optional.
